To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the dark sector interactions are not constrained by the current cosmological observations; 2) the dark sector interaction can lead to a nontrivial future evolution of the universe; 3) the future cosmological observations can be helpful in constraining the interaction between dark matter and the dark energy; 4) the dark sector couplings are not ruled out by the current cosmology.

1) The cosmological dynamics of a wide class of models with nongradiational couplings between the dark sector components can be described by a single effective scalar field with a nonstandard kinetic term.

(i) the dark sector is not a closed system; (ii) the dark energy equation of state can be different from the cosmological constant; and (iii) the dark sector interactions can be constrained by observations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following topics:

the study of the cosmological evolution of the Universe, and the possible implications for the structure formation and the cosmic microwave background radiation anisotropies, in models with nongravitationally coupled dark sectors.
a wide range of problems related to dark matter, dark energy and their mutual interactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the dark sector interactions are not yet excluded by the observational constraints, but they are still not favoured by them.
the cosmological evolution is sensitive to interactions in the dark sector.
there is no evidence of any interaction in the dark sector, and that there is a strong indication for the existence of dark matter, but no evidence for dark energy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dark energy is a dynamical field, and the dark matter is a dynamical component of the dark energy, and the dark energy and the dark matter interact with each other.
, in the presence of nongravitating dark matter and dark matter, the dark matter is not a dark matter.
the dark energy equation of state is not a constant but a function of time, and that the dark matter is not stable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dark sector interactions can have a strong influence on cosmological observations.
the dark sector interactions may be probed with future cosmological observations.
the future evolution of our universe is not necessarily dominated by the cosmological constant.
